- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#5 ("Confirm the paper's Method account against your code") by `experiment-repo`  > Checked `paper/sections/method.tex` (dev @ 2c55526) against the code at HEAD (analysis/core.py, protocols.py, decisions.py, intervals.py, experiments/real_gap.py, run_protocols.py, assemble.py). Corrections and answers:
  > 
  > **Confirmed as written:** K=128 space and scoring (log-prob of each valid option letter, -inf for invalid ones, argmax; demo rows are dropped in `assemble.py`, so they are in neither S nor the truth); default config c=0; random / hill-climb / SH descriptions; κ, refined predictor, K_eff (Blom inversion of κ); optimism bootstrap (100 resamples) and .632 formulas; nested cross-fit; split and its exact (Clopper–Pearson) bound; pool-bootstrap interval with the MC variance removed.
  > 
  > **Corrections / precision needed**
  > 1. *N−n ≥ 1100* holds only at n = 400 (gap-vs-n). In the protocol experiments N_tot ≤ 240, so the fresh set has ≥ 1260 items (SE ≤ 0.014). Say "N−n ≥ 1100 (n ≤ 400)" or give it per experiment. The pool is 1500 non-demo items (pool.pkl has 1512 rows, 12 demos flagged and removed): confirmed.
  > 2. *Candidate set "evaluated" for successive halving* is the set that survives to the **last round (2 configurations)**, not all configurations ever scored (all 128 are scored in round 1, on a small subset). So max-t/Bonferroni over "evaluated" for SH is a deliberately too-narrow set; "declared" is the valid one. Say this; for random search "evaluated" = the B drawn, for hill-climb = the distinct configurations visited.
  > 3. *Max-t lower bound*: q uses the item-level column SD of each candidate in the denominator (multiplier bootstrap, B=500 draws); the width factor is the **binomial** se of the selected configuration, sqrt(p(1−p)/n) with p(1−p) floored at 1/(4n), not an item-level se of its own. For 0/1 columns these agree except for the floor. In the decisions the same q is computed on the paired differences to the default, over the declared set.
  > 4. *Bonferroni*: z_{1−α/m} only. The unused Šidák quantile was dead code and I removed it; the paper reports Bonferroni only. I also run `pointwise_lb` (ĉ's one-sided z bound with no multiplicity adjustment) as the unadjusted reference; add one clause naming it if you show it.
  > 5. *Scoring on the real matrix*: "cons" = point report > fresh + 1.645·se (overstatement) or bound ≤ fresh + 1.645·se (coverage): it is the scoring more favourable to the protocol; "anticons" is against the measured fresh accuracy itself. A statement is "valid/invalid" only if both agree. Synthetic worlds have exact θ and one coverage, plus a `*_noisy` check that adds fresh-set noise to θ.
  > 6. *Decision tests*: the naive and split tests are paired z-tests with the sample SD (ddof 1) of the per-item difference; the split test uses a 50/50 split of S. Fine as written, but "claims that tuning helped" = declared when z > 1.645.
  > 7. *Counts*: the real protocol and decision runs will use the original pool (2000 draws of U) plus R pool-bootstrap replicates × 200 draws; R is set by the compute that is left, **not 200** as the Method says for the gap experiments. Only the gap-vs-n and C2 driver runs use 200 replicates × 100 draws plus the original pool at 2000 draws. I will give R per file in `code/results/README.md`; leave the number out of the Method until then.
  > 8. New column for the n = 400 request from story-repo: `gap_vs_pool` (reported minus accuracy of ĉ on the whole pool, S included) next to `gap` (against pool∖S). Mean gap against pool∖S is (N/(N−n)) × the whole-pool gap for a fixed config, so the n = 400 point is 1.36× its whole-pool reading; the between-pool interval already contains this. Say in the text which one the point is.
  > 9. *Not yet in the Method*: C7 (semi-synthetic: `analysis/semisynth.py` is in dev; its experiment runner is not yet written) and the leakage counterfactual (`experiments/matrix_facts.py`, Δ_leak; the counterfactual blocks are `cf.npz`, computed already). I will post here when their results land; the code is at the paths above.
